history.motion: Plain scroll with a sticky header and rotated margin label; no reveals, no easing visible, restrained to the point of static.
history.verdict: A is a quiet, consistent editorial ledger with a coherent hairline system (solid rows, gold dashed groups) and clean small caps, but it never rises above competent and its inconsistent tickers and dead band keep it off a shortlist. B has the atmosphere and photographic ambition of a stronger site, yet illegible copy over imagery, a logo collision, missing-space text bugs and a struck-through mobile nav are craft failures a jury cannot forgive, so the restrained one wins.

history.gap: Every row is the same height and every market name is the same size and weight, so a genuinely good idea flattens into a table — "Olie" alone in a full-width band is void, not tension. The superscript tickers are applied inconsistently (NQ, ES, XAUUSD present; nothing on Zilver, Olie, Bitcoin, Altcoins), which reads as an oversight rather than a rule. Vary row rhythm and name scale by group weight, and either tag all eight markets or none.
history.verdict: B takes it narrowly, and on idea rather than execution. It is the only one of the two doing something I have not seen a hundred times: a markets index set as an editorial masthead in high-contrast serif, prices deliberately withheld and that refusal stated in the caption, held together by gold hairlines, letterspaced category rails and a numbered section convention. Colour restraint is exemplary — ink, bone, one gold, one italic accent — and the mobile stack survives the reduction better than the desktop does. A is the higher-craft object: its motion sheet is the best work on the table and its mobile Work page is confidently set. But the desktop frame is a hole with pictures clipped around the edges and a floating hover pill, and the aesthetic is the default award-site dialect executed very well rather than a position of its own. B loses motion outright and its uniform row rhythm undercuts the concept badly; fix the rhythm and choreograph the section entry and it moves into shortlist range. Neither is there as-is.
